title: Best free AI to use for making games?
author: Zealousideal-Pen7888
selftext:
Hey y'all, most games online just don't do it for me anymore so I figured why not just make my own. Only problem is I have zero game dev experience and don't really want to spend months learning Unity or whatever.

Been messing around with a few AI tools and some of them are actually surprisingly decent. Didn't expect to get something playable so fast. Anyone else doing this just for fun? What are you using?

comments.author: Kingnorik
comments.body: You're going to have to pay. But the new Claude opus Fable is pretty insane in what it can cook up from one prompt.

replies.author: ai-ghtman
replies.body: Any experience on it generating models or even textures? Opus keeps directing me to 3rd party resources for this.

replies.author: SquirrelTomahawk
replies.body: Textures? Thats not really claude or codex job...

replies.author: SquirrelTomahawk
replies.body: Yeah i made the switch to codex from claude now i tested fable and im back to claude 🫩

replies.author: Zeiban
replies.body: The best thing about Fable being released is that the other models will become cheaper.  From what I've read from reviews Fable is overkill in many situations we're a cheaper model will work fine.

comments.author: North_Equipment_6737
comments.body: honestly if you just want to make something fun for yourself without learning game dev, there's no shame in using free ai tools. you're not trying to compete, just create. the limitations might actually force you to be more creative with scope.

comments.author: 0bscuris
comments.body:
It’s fun! A fun hobby. 

But To do anything right takes time. Ai speeds up the mundane tasks like what i would call sinew code, the code that makes that button work, for example but the time you save on that, you need to spend on upfront design and in the back end in testing. Ai produces alot of work quickly but in the same way that if you ask it to write a story or do a picture you can immediately spot problems in it, same with the code you don’t understand. 

unity asset flips are shit games, ai is just an evolution of that. It can make fast shit games. It’s the justifiable part of why people don’t like ai games. 

Back when i used to do game jams, u’d have a working prototype like the first day, the whole second day would be spent trying to make it not suck. Same thing here.

replies.author: Zealousideal-Pen7888
replies.body: Fair point. AI doesn't save the hard part, it just speeds up the grunt work. You still need solid design upfront and a full pass to make it not feel half-baked. Fast production can actually hurt if you're just shipping the first draft.

comments.author: Smilysis
comments.body:
You want it for free? then use your brain and learn how to code 😭

There are no free alternatives, but you could try opencode go, their models are decent when it comes to coding

replies.author: Prettypeachrec
replies.body: Honestly you can get A LOT from just $20

replies.author: Smilysis
replies.body:
Yes, codex is also very good

There's no escape on spending money when it comes to ai coding, but imo it's worth

comments.author: M4xs0n
comments.body: Bro at least decide which Engine you wanna use and and then learn it by using AI. You have no idea what you are doing, found out AI can do Crazy stuff already and now want to create your own games like it’s not a big deal. The coding part is the easy part and AI can totally do that for you but give it access to your whole projects context all the time. The hard part is having a great idea, working on it and don’t stop until its done. That’s the part AI can‘t do for you.

comments.author: ShiftyShankerton
comments.body: Claude to make python systems for a custom narrative simulation engine that actually tracks narrative state writes to disk and uses it for the loop. The llm can be anything api or local models. The llm in this system is not running everything they are interpreting the json packets the system feeds it. I am just working on polishing it.

comments.author: Hefty-Egg132
comments.body: The better question is what kind of game. Making a narrative game with AI-generated visuals and branching choices is way more achievable right now than trying to make a 3D action game with free tools. Pick a genre that actually plays to what AI is good at instead of fighting against limitations.

replies.author: Zealousideal-Pen7888
replies.body:
This is the actual answer. Narrative games with branching choices align way better with what AI can do right now. Trying to make a 3D action game with free tools is fighting uphill.

If you're exploring this space, lean into story, dialogue, choices, maybe some lighter puzzle elements. That's where you'll see results fast instead of grinding for months.

comments.author: Am_Biyori
comments.body: As a follow up question: How much money are we talking? If you're using it for both coding and art? Is there a price difference between using it for just art or just coding?

comments.author: leobesat
comments.body:
depends on what type of game you want to make. If it's story-heavy with branching dialogue, you want something focused on narrative. If it's asset generation for a 3D game you're making yourself, that's a different tool. Free tools tend to do one thing okay rather than everything well.

Also be realistic about 'playable' with free tiers. You might get a prototype but actually shipping something requires either money or serious optimization work.

replies.author: Zealousideal-Pen7888
replies.body: Real talk. You can get to prototype with free stuff but shipping anything actually polished takes either money or a ton of optimization work. Free tiers are great for testing if an idea even works, not for finishing a full game.

comments.author: Elpepestan
comments.body: Free AI tools are deceptive because they work great for the first prototype then hit rate limits or quality drops the second you try to scale. The real answer is pick one tool and go paid if it works. You'll waste more time hopping between free tiers than you would just paying for the one that actually gets you where you want to go.

comments.author: Zeiban
comments.body:
Realistically, there isn't a real free option out there. 

Local LLMs are a thing but you have to have the hardware to run them.  My 5090 processes more tokens these days than rendering polygons.  

Lot of providers will have limited free usage but you hit that very quickly. Even the $20 a month plans you burn through pretty quickly.

Every industry that uses AI is starting to see the cost involved as providers run out of VC it actually have to start making a profit.

comments.author: last1031
comments.body: you could just have free tier claude generate code for you and put it together. but if you dont know how to do it yourself it make get confusing.

comments.author: RivenTries
comments.body: The biggest surprise for me was how quickly AI lets you test ideas. Instead of wondering whether a mechanic will work, you can usually have a rough version running the same day
